edbDesc: (SAW) An acoustic wave traveling along the surface of a material having some elasticity, with an amplitude that typically decays exponentially with the depth of the substrate. This kind of wave is commonly used in devices called SAW devices in electronics circuits.
title: Surface acoustic wave
description: Sound can run along the skin of a solid like a ripple on a pond, staying near the surface instead of going through. Rayleigh predicted these waves in 1885 to explain earthquake shaking; ripples on piezoelectric chips now filter radio signals in every mobile phone.
effect: sound travels as a ripple along the surface of a solid
usedIn: SAW radio filters in mobile phones
strength: On a chip the ripples are only a few atoms tall and travel at about 3 kilometres per second, but they can sort radio channels precisely and even push droplets around.
pickWhy: Specific named effect with large commercial use; also called Rayleigh waves.
